name: Amanda Padilla
background: Amanda Padilla is a Jackson entrepreneur who ran as the Libertarian nominee for Senate District 17 in 2022. She lost the Nov. 8, 2022 general election.

In an Oct. 26, 2022 Jackson Hole News&Guide candidate feature, Padilla described herself as an entrepreneur from an early age, recalling that as a Girl Scout she sold more than 1,200 boxes of cookies. The same column identified her as the youngest candidate in that Senate District 17 field. Her 2022 Secretary of State general-election filing listed a Jackson mailing address.

name: Bethany Baldes
occupation: Real estate agent; president of the Riverton Chamber of Commerce (as of November 2022)
background: Bethany Baldes is a lifelong Riverton resident who ran as the Libertarian nominee for House District 55 in 2022. She lost the Nov. 8, 2022 general election to incumbent Ember Oakley. It was her third race for the seat: WyoFile reported that she lost to then-Rep. David Miller by 53 votes in 2018 and to Oakley by 32 votes in 2020.

A Nov. 4, 2022 WyoFile report said that after serving in the Wyoming National Guard, Baldes was a stay-at-home mother for 11 years, and that she was then working as a real estate agent and serving as president of the Riverton Chamber of Commerce. A WyoFile author biography has also described her as a community activist and mother of three who served six years in the Wyoming Army National Guard and later founded Local Ladies, a social-media outlet highlighting Fremont County businesses.
military: Wyoming Army National Guard (six years, per a WyoFile author biography)

name: Bob Strobel
occupation: Owner of See Jackson Hole and the Jackson Hole Computer Clinic; co-founder and former vice president of Jackson Hole Net
background: Bob Strobel is an Etna resident who ran as an independent for House District 22 in 2022, seeking the seat left open when Rep. Jim Roscoe did not run again. He lost the Nov. 8, 2022 general election. His 2022 campaign site said he moved to Jackson Hole from Twin Falls, Idaho, in 1995 at age 19, to be closer to his grandmother and the family ranch in Bondurant. He wrote that he co-founded Jackson Hole Net (later AllTrips.com) and served as vice president for 18 years before starting See Jackson Hole, a live-webcam tourism site, and that he also owns and manages the Jackson Hole Computer Clinic in Jackson.

A June 8, 2022 Jackson Hole News&Guide report identified him as 47 years old at the time of that interview, said he and his wife of 16 years had a 7-year-old son and a 6-year-old daughter, and noted that outgoing Rep. Roscoe had endorsed him. WyoFile’s Oct. 15, 2022 race preview likewise described him as an Etna resident and founder of SeeJH.com and the Jackson Hole Computer Clinic. His campaign site named his wife as Clara Harbeck and said the family lived in Etna full time.

name: Marissa Joy Selvig
occupation: Self-employed musician and worship leader; director of the free food pantry for Foundations for Nations Ministries (as of September 2022)
background: Marissa Joy Selvig of Riverton ran as the Constitution Party nominee for Wyoming’s U.S. House seat in 2022 and lost the Nov. 8, 2022 general election.

In a Sept. 28, 2022 Wyoming Tribune Eagle candidate questionnaire, Selvig said she was 39, lived in Riverton, had been married 16 years, and was the mother of four. She listed a bachelor of science in Speech Communication–Theatre Arts, with a minor in Musical Theatre Performance, from the University of Wisconsin–River Falls; service on Pavillion’s town council (2017–2019) and as mayor (2019–2020); and a then-current role as chair of Riverton’s EDGE committee. She also described herself as a self-employed musician, a worship leader, director of the free food pantry for Foundations for Nations Ministries, and an avid gardener.

name: Todd Peterson
occupation: Retired rural banker; former president of Pinnacle Bank in Torrington (retired 2021)
background: Todd Peterson is a Goshen County native who ran as an independent for House District 5 in 2022. He lost the Nov. 8, 2022 general election. His Secretary of State general-election filing listed a Torrington mailing address.

A Sept. 10, 2022 KNEB / Rural Radio announcement said Peterson was raised in Goshen County, graduated from the University of Wyoming with a degree in agricultural economics, and had worked more than 40 years in rural banking, beginning with Farm Credit and retiring in 2021 after 22 years with Pinnacle Bank, including service as president of Pinnacle Bank in Torrington. The same announcement said he served on Goshen Economic Development (including as a past president), the Wyoming Lottery Commission, the Eastern Wyoming College Foundation board, and the St. Joseph’s board, and that he was a past president of the Torrington Rotary club. It also said he graduated from Leadership Wyoming in 2006, and that he and his late wife Maggie, married 41 years, had four children and seven grandchildren.
education: Degree in agricultural economics, University of Wyoming
prior_offices: Wyoming Lottery Commission; Past president, Goshen Economic Development
